source_group: classic and practitioner swing methods (beyond docs/methods.md)

conventions.evidence_grade: A = strong peer-reviewed multi-market; B = peer-reviewed/independent and consistent; C = independent or descriptive tests, mixed or not cost-inclusive; D = originator claims/anecdote only; none = definition or nothing found
conventions.formula_status: exact = rules as published (restated in own words); approximation = parameters partly unverified or adapted; description_only = discretionary method
conventions.free_data_ok: implementable with daily OHLCV plus free SEC/FINRA/Alpha Vantage data
conventions.ticks: Futures 'ticks' in the originals map to a few cents or ~0.05-0.1% of price for stocks

not_duplicated: RSI(2), Double 7s, Cumulative RSI, R3, ConnorsRSI, ConnorsRSI Pullback, Alpha Formula (methods/11); Holy Grail and Landry pullback core (methods/01); turn-of-month seasonality, Weinstein/Turtle Soup one-liners (methods.md 1b) - only missing rules added.

items.name: Turtle Soup (long; short is the mirror)
items.brand_or_source: Linda Bradford Raschke & Laurence Connors, Street Smarts (1995)
items.rules_or_formula: Setup: today trades to a new 20-day low (the lower the better) AND the previous 20-day low was printed at least 4 sessions earlier. Entry: once price is below that prior 20-day low, place a buy stop 5-10 ticks above the prior 20-day low, valid today only. Stop: if filled, protective sell stop 1 tick under today's low. Management: trail the stop as the trade becomes profitable; a fade of failed Donchian-20 breakouts. Hold hours to a few days. Short: new 20-day high, prior 20-day high >= 4 sessions earlier, sell stop 5-10 ticks below it.
items.entry: Intraday stop re-entry into the range on the breakout day
items.daily_bar_implementation: On day t: prior20low = min(low[t-20..t-1]) with its date <= t-4; if low_t < prior20low and high_t >= prior20low + buffer, assume fill at prior20low + buffer (order-of-fill ambiguity: the low printed before the fill by construction). Stop = low_t - tick. Buffer: use 0.05-0.10% of price or 1-2 cents for stocks (ticks are a futures concept).
items.evidence: No independent, cost-inclusive test located; restatements quote book rules only. Existing methods.md row rates it D (regime dependent, poor in persistent trends).
items.overlap_with_methods_md: Listed one-line in methods.md section 1b (Turtle Soup failed-breakout reversal); this adds the exact rules.

items.name: Turtle Soup Plus One
items.brand_or_source: Raschke & Connors, Street Smarts (1995)
items.rules_or_formula: Day 1: market makes a new 20-day low, the previous 20-day low was at least 3 sessions earlier, and day 1 CLOSES at or below that previous 20-day low. Day 2: place a buy stop at the earlier 20-day low; cancel if not filled on day 2. Stop: below the lower of day-1/day-2 lows (common restatement). Trail as for Turtle Soup. Shorts mirror on 20-day highs.
items.entry: Day-2 buy stop at the prior 20-day low
items.stop: Under the lower of the two days' lows
items.daily_bar_implementation: Fully codeable on daily bars: signal at close of day 1, stop-entry level known before day 2 open; if open_2 > level, fill at open.
items.evidence: Only originator claims and anecdotal success rates (55-65% wins in unsourced restatements). No audited test.
items.unverified: Exact initial stop wording not checked against the book this run.

items.name: 80-20 reversal
items.brand_or_source: Raschke & Connors, Street Smarts (1995)
items.rules_or_formula: Buy setup: yesterday OPENED in the top 20% of its high-low range and CLOSED in the bottom 20%. Today price must trade at least 5-15 ticks below yesterday's low (guideline). Entry: buy stop at yesterday's low (price re-enters the prior range). Stop: near today's low; move it up to lock in profit. Taught as a day trade; can be held if strong. Sell setup mirrors (open bottom 20%, close top 20%, trade above yesterday's high, sell stop at yesterday's high). Rationale: Taylor-style statistic that such bars usually see follow-through beyond the extreme next morning, which then often fails.
items.entry: Stop at prior day's low after a flush below it
items.exit: Same day or next 1-2 days; trail
items.daily_bar_implementation: Setup flag from prior bar: (open - low)/(high - low) >= 0.8 and (close - low)/(high - low) <= 0.2. Fill if low_t < prevLow - buffer and high_t >= prevLow.
items.evidence: Originator claims only; no independent test found.
items.unverified: Rules from a search summary of the book; Roboforex gives a different, forex-adapted version (80% body candle) that is NOT the book rule.

items.name: Momentum Pinball (LBR/RSI)
items.brand_or_source: Raschke & Connors, Street Smarts (1995)
items.rules_or_formula: Indicator LBR/RSI = 3-period RSI of the 1-day rate of change (close minus prior close). Signal: if LBR/RSI closes below 30, look to buy tomorrow; above 70, look to short. Next day: let the first trading hour set a range; buy stop above the first-hour high (short: sell stop below first-hour low). Stop at the opposite side of the first-hour range. If losing at the close, exit; if profitable or flat, carry overnight and exit the next day on the follow-through. Never hold a second night. Re-entry allowed if stopped and the range breaks again. Prefer instruments with good average daily range.
items.entry: Next-day first-hour range breakout in signal direction
items.daily_bar_implementation: Signal is daily. Entry needs 60-minute bars; daily approximation (buy stop above prior-day high) changes the method - flag as approximation if used.
items.evidence: Authors' claim that it 'can't be beaten' for 1-2 day flips; no independent test located.

items.name: The Anti (stochastic hook pullback)
items.brand_or_source: Linda Bradford Raschke (Street Smarts; LBR manual)
items.rules_or_formula: Stochastic with %K period 7, %K smoothing 4 and %D (slow line) 10 per Street Smarts (Raschke's later manual uses %D 12). Buy: %D has established an uptrend (rising for roughly 4+ bars); %K pulls back toward/against %D for about 3+ bars; enter when %K hooks back up in the direction of %D (buy stop above the hook bar). Stop just below the entry bar low or last swing low. Exit within 2-4 bars. Sells mirror. Idea: early re-entry after a failed counter-trend move.
items.entry: Hook of fast line back in the slow line's direction
items.daily_bar_implementation: Codeable on daily bars: slowK = SMA4(fastK7); slowD = SMA10(slowK); conditions on slopes over the last 3-4 bars.
items.evidence: No independent test located.
items.unverified: Bar counts (4 and 3) come from forum restatements, not the book text.

items.name: Holy Grail (missing rules only)
items.brand_or_source: Raschke & Connors, Street Smarts (1995)
items.rules_or_formula: 14-period ADX initially above 30 and rising; price retraces to the 20-period moving average (EMA in most restatements, SMA in tradingsetupsreview); buy stop at/above the high of the bar that touches the MA; stop at the newly formed swing low; first target is a retest of the recent swing high; trail if the trend continues. The book also covers re-entry and a second retracement. Known drawbacks: high ADX can mean an overdone trend; slow steady trends may never push ADX above 30.
items.entry: Buy stop over the MA-touch bar
items.daily_bar_implementation: Needs adx_14 (+DI/-DI) feature - already proposed in methods/01.
items.evidence: No independent cost-inclusive test of the exact rules (methods/01). Pullback-in-trend family is B- there.
items.overlap_with_methods_md: Covered in methods/01; only the drawbacks and re-entry note are new.

items.name: Connors %b strategy (ETF)
items.brand_or_source: Larry Connors, High Probability ETF Trading (2009), ch. 5
items.rules_or_formula: Long: close above the 200-day moving average; Bollinger %b below 0.2 for 3 consecutive days; buy on the close. Exit when %b closes above 0.8. Aggressive version adds on further oversold readings (unverified). Shorts mirror below the 200-day with %b above 0.8 for 3 days, exit below 0.2. %b = (close - lower band)/(upper band - lower band).
items.entry: Close after 3 days of %b < 0.2
items.daily_bar_implementation: Codeable on daily bars. Band length/width used by Connors not confirmed this run - test 20/2 and short settings (e.g., 5-day) side by side.
items.evidence: Connors tested 20 ETFs from inception to end-2008 (in-sample). Quantified Strategies re-test (paywalled) noted good results in SPY/QQQ but very few fills.
items.unverified: Band parameters and the aggressive scale-in rule not confirmed.
items.overlap_with_methods_md: Not in methods/11 (which covers RSI-2, Double 7s, Cumulative RSI, R3, ConnorsRSI).

items.name: Connors 3-Day High/Low method (ETF)
items.brand_or_source: Larry Connors, High Probability ETF Trading (2009), strategy 1
items.rules_or_formula: Long: close above the 200-day SMA; close below the 5-day SMA; three consecutive days of lower highs AND lower lows (high[t] < high[t-1] < high[t-2] < high[t-3] and the same for lows); buy on the close. Aggressive version: add a second unit if the ETF closes below the entry price while in the trade (unverified). Exit on the first close above the 5-day SMA. Shorts mirror (below 200-day, above 5-day, three higher highs and higher lows).
items.entry: Close
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exactly codeable. Note EdgeRater's listing has a typo (today's high vs prior low); use high<prior high and low<prior low.
items.evidence: EdgeRater replication on Connors' 20 ETFs, 1993-2008: 4-day forward returns after the entry beat a random-entry baseline (baseline mean +0.094%, SD 3.48%); no cost-inclusive equity curve.
items.unverified: Aggressive add-on rule.

items.name: Connors TPS (Time, Price, Scale-in)
items.brand_or_source: Larry Connors, High Probability ETF Trading (2009)
items.rules_or_formula: Long only while the ETF is above its 200-day moving average. Setup: 2-period RSI below 25 for two consecutive days -> buy 10% of the intended position at the close. Each later close below the previous entry price -> add 20%, then 30%, then 40% (10+20+30+40 = 100%). Exit the whole position when RSI(2) closes above 70. Scaling stops if price loses the 200-day MA.
items.entry: Close; scale 10/20/30/40%
items.stop: None (time and scale-in replace the stop)
items.daily_bar_implementation: Codeable; position-size state machine needed. Risk: averaging down concentrates exposure into a falling instrument - cap total size.
items.evidence: Originator claims; no independent test located. Negative-skew profile like all Connors MR (methods/11).
items.unverified: One restatement says 200-day EMA; Connors normally uses SMA.
items.overlap_with_methods_md: methods/11 mentions TPS only as 'unverified'; this confirms the 10/20/30/40 scale and RSI(2) 25/70 thresholds.

items.name: Connors HPETF other rules (RSI(4) 25/75, Multiple Days Down, RSI 10/6)
items.brand_or_source: Larry Connors, High Probability ETF Trading (2009)
items.rules_or_formula: From recollection of the book, NOT verified this run: (a) RSI 25/75: above 200-day MA, 4-period RSI closes below 25 -> buy close; aggressive add if RSI(4) < 20; exit RSI(4) > 55. (b) Multiple Days Up/Down: above 200-day MA, close below 5-day MA, down closes on 4 of the last 5 days -> buy close; aggressive add on a lower close; exit close above 5-day MA. (c) RSI 10/6: above 200-day MA, RSI(2) < 10 buy, add if RSI(2) < 6; exit close above 5-day MA.
items.entry: Close
items.daily_bar_implementation: Codeable; verify thresholds against the book before use.
items.evidence: None verified.
items.unverified: All thresholds in this item.

items.name: Oops! (gap-through reversal)
items.brand_or_source: Larry Williams, Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading (1999), ch. 7
items.rules_or_formula: Buy: today OPENS below yesterday's low (gap through support); place a buy stop at (a tick above) yesterday's low the same day - the fill means the gap failed. Sell: open above yesterday's high, sell stop at yesterday's high. Williams applied it selectively (e.g., S&P 'Oops' chapter, day-of-week filters). Typical exits: protective stop at the day's extreme; exit at the close or on the first profitable open (Williams' 'bailout' idea, unverified pairing).
items.entry: Stop at prior day's low after a gap below it
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact on daily bars: if open_t < low_{t-1} and high_t >= low_{t-1} -> fill at low_{t-1} (or open if open >= level, impossible here).
items.evidence: Book examples only; a widely repeated '93% of the time' gap-fill claim has no traceable test. Gap-fill base rates for small index gaps are high (see gap item) but Oops requires a full gap through the prior low.

items.name: Smash Day reversal (naked) and Hidden Smash Day
items.brand_or_source: Larry Williams, Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading (1999), ch. 7
items.rules_or_formula: Naked smash (buy): a down day that closes BELOW the prior day's low (often taking out several recent lows); if price next trades above the smash day's high, buy (buy stop 1 tick over its high); stop under the smash-day low. Hidden smash (buy): an UP close (close > prior close) that nevertheless closes in the lowest 25% of its own range ((close - low) <= 0.25 x (high - low)); buy stop above its high next day; stop under its low. Sells mirror (close above prior high; or down close in top 25% of range). The buy stop is usually left for the next 1-3 days (author does not fix a duration).
items.entry: Buy stop above smash-day high
items.exit: Trail / short swing; Williams also used time exits
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact on daily bars. Best used in the direction of the higher-timeframe trend (smash as end of pullback).
items.evidence: Originator examples only.

items.name: Williams volatility breakout and Greatest Swing Value
items.brand_or_source: Larry Williams (Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading, ch. 4)
items.rules_or_formula: Volatility breakout: buy stop at today's OPEN + k x (yesterday's range or true range); sell stop at open - k x range; k is chosen by testing (broker adaptations use 0.25 of the prior high-low; Korean retail version uses k about 0.5-0.6 on the prior range). Greatest Swing Value (GSV) variant: noise on an up-close day = open - low, on a down-close day = high - open (min of both when close = open); GSV = SMA_N(noise) x multiple; buy stop at open + GSV, sell stop at open - GSV; first filled is the position, the other is the protective stop. Exits: protective stop, time exit, or Williams' bailout (exit at the first profitable opening).
items.entry: Stop order at open +/- k*range
items.daily_bar_implementation: Codeable with daily OHLC if fills are simulated at the stop level when high/low crosses it; ambiguous days where both stops trade need a rule (Oxford Capital assumes worst case).
items.evidence: Oxford Capital Strategies benchmarked ORB/GSV variants on 42 futures, 1980-2011, with sensitivity grids (numbers not captured). No stock-swing test found.
items.unverified: Williams' own k values were not read this run.

items.name: Williams %R
items.brand_or_source: Larry Williams
items.rules_or_formula: %R = (highest high_n - close) / (highest high_n - lowest low_n) x -100; default n = 14 (ChartSchool). Range 0 to -100: above -20 overbought, below -80 oversold, -50 centreline. Signals: in uptrends buy oversold readings that turn back up through -50; 'momentum failure' when %R can no longer reach -20 (or -80). 125-day %R approximates a 6-month trend gauge. Elder uses %R below -80 as a second-screen buy condition in an uptrend.
items.evidence: No peer-reviewed test of %R rules verified.

items.name: Williams VIX Fix (synthetic VIX)
items.brand_or_source: Larry Williams, Active Trader (Dec 2007)
items.rules_or_formula: WVF = (highest CLOSE over the last 22 bars - today's LOW) / highest close over 22 bars x 100. Spikes mark fear/capitulation lows for any index, ETF or stock (no options data needed); 22 = max trading days in a month (26 suggested on weekly). Common use: WVF above its upper Bollinger band (20, 2) or above its 50-bar percentile as an oversold trigger for mean-reversion buys in uptrends.
items.evidence: No independent test verified; useful stock-level stand-in for the VIX filter in Connors' rules (methods/11).
items.unverified: The Bollinger/percentile trigger is a common community add-on, not Williams' text.

items.name: Williams market-structure swing points
items.brand_or_source: Larry Williams, Long-Term Secrets to Short-Term Trading (1999), ch. 1
items.rules_or_formula: Short-term low = a daily low with higher lows on both sides; short-term high = a high with lower highs on both sides. Ignore inside days (range inside prior day). Outside days need the open-to-close path to decide which extreme came first. Intermediate-term low = a short-term low with higher short-term lows on both sides; long-term low = an intermediate low with higher intermediate lows on both sides (mirror for highs). Real-time: a short-term low is confirmed once price rallies above the high of a day that made a lower low than its prior day. Frequencies in his 50,692-session study of 9 commodities: inside days 3,892 (7.6%), outside days 3,487.
items.evidence: Definition, not a strategy; primary excerpt.
items.overlap_with_methods_md: Useful for swing_high/swing_low targets and stops already used by pullback_trend.

items.name: NR4 / NR7 range-contraction breakout
items.brand_or_source: Toby Crabel, Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout (1990)
items.rules_or_formula: NR7 = today's absolute range (high - low) is the narrowest of the last 7 days (smaller than each of the prior 6); NR4 = narrowest of the last 4. Trade the next-day break: buy above the NR day's high, sell below its low; Crabel took profits fast (close of the entry day or first profitable close). Failure to follow through at once is the first warning; a move back through the other side negates. ChartSchool filtered version: NR7 that is also inside the prior day, Aroon Up(63) > Aroon Down(63), and min(CCI(10), 5 days) < -100 (uptrend after pullback).
items.entry: Stop above NR-day high
items.exit: Close of day 1 / first profitable close, or 7% target per Bulkowski test
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact on daily bars.
items.evidence: Bulkowski, 1,201 stocks Jan 1990-Mar 2013: bull-market up-breakout failure rate 46%, measure rule met 43%; a 7% target / 7% stop test ($10 commissions, 29,021 trades across all conditions) in bull-market up-breakouts won 57% (7,600 winners, 5,791 losers) for an average net +$78.79 per $10,000 trade (~+0.8%), average hold 31 calendar days. Oxford Capital (42 futures, 1980-2011): NR7 + ORB 'not currently tradeable' after costs without extra rules.
items.overlap_with_methods_md: Mentioned inside methods/09 (Stockbee) as an NR7/NR4 precursor; here as a standalone entry.

items.name: ID/NR4 (inside day + NR4)
items.brand_or_source: Toby Crabel; popularised by Raschke & Connors, Street Smarts
items.rules_or_formula: Setup: an inside day (high < prior high and low > prior low) that is also an NR4. Next day: buy stop 1 tick above the ID/NR4 high and sell stop 1 tick below its low; whichever fills is the position and the other order becomes the stop (stop-and-reverse allowed). Exit fast if the expansion does not come (same day or within 1-2 days); trail when it does.
items.entry: OCO stops around the ID/NR4 bar
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact on daily bars except same-day reversals.
items.evidence: No separate test found; see NR4/NR7 item.
items.unverified: Street Smarts' exact exit wording not read.

items.name: Crabel opening-range breakout with 'stretch' (daily-bar swing entry)
items.brand_or_source: Toby Crabel (1990); S&C 'Opening Range Breakout' series 1988-89
items.rules_or_formula: Noise_i = min(high_i - open_i, open_i - low_i) (distance from open to the nearer extreme). Stretch = SMA over the prior 10 days of noise (x multiple). Each day: buy stop at open + stretch, sell stop at open - stretch; the first filled is the position and the other is the protective stop. Crabel used it most on days after contraction patterns (NR4, NR7, ID/NR4, two-bar NR) where expansion is expected. Swing use: enter on the ORB trigger the day after a contraction day, hold for the expansion move.
items.entry: Stop at open +/- stretch
items.exit: Close of day / time index / ATR stop
items.daily_bar_implementation: Codeable with daily OHLC (the open is known; simulate stop fills).
items.evidence: Oxford Capital ran ORB sensitivity tests on 42 futures 1980-2011 (numbers not captured). methods.md: intraday ORB in stocks nets about 0 after costs.
items.overlap_with_methods_md: methods.md avoid-bucket lists intraday ORB day trading; this is the daily-bar swing use.

items.name: Hit and Run 'Hit List' stock filter
items.brand_or_source: Jeff Cooper, Hit and Run Trading (1996; updated ed. 2004)
items.rules_or_formula: Trade only stocks with ADX > 30 (14-period assumed) (or IBD Relative Strength > 95 if ADX is not used). Longs only when price is above both the 10-day and 50-day MAs; shorts only below both. Longs should be at a 4-week (or 2-month) high, shorts at a 4-week low. Price above $30 (prefers $40+); minor criterion: average volume >= 200,000 shares.
items.evidence: Author's track record and examples only.
items.unverified: From a Vietnamese summary of the book; the $30 floor reflects 1990s prices.

items.name: 1-2-3-4 pullback (Hit and Run 1-2-3 Pullbacks)
items.brand_or_source: Jeff Cooper, Hit and Run Trading; co-taught with Connors/Raschke
items.rules_or_formula: Stock on the hit list (ADX > 30 with +DI > -DI for longs). It pulls back with three consecutive lower lows (inside days are not counted). Day 4: buy when price trades above the high of day 3 (buy stop a tick over it). Stop below the day-3 (pullback) low. Exit into strength over the next days (Cooper scales out / trails). Shorts mirror (ADX > 30, -DI > +DI, three higher highs, sell below day-3 low).
items.entry: Buy stop above day-3 high
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact on daily bars; needs ADX/DI feature.
items.evidence: No independent test; same family as the Holy Grail and Connors 3-day pullbacks (methods/01).

items.name: Expansion Pivot
items.brand_or_source: Jeff Cooper, Hit and Run Trading, ch. 8
items.rules_or_formula: Buy: today's range is larger than the range of each of the previous 9 sessions; yesterday or today the stock was at or below its 50-day MA and today it bursts up through/above the 50-day MA. Next day: buy 1/8 point (today: a few cents) above the expansion day's high. Stop just below the expansion day's low. Short mirror: largest range in 10 days breaking down through the 50-day MA. Book example: IBM, 18 Jan 1995 (buy above 96 1/4, stop under 95 1/4).
items.entry: Next-day stop above expansion-day high
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact on daily bars: range_t > max(range_{t-9..t-1}); min(low_{t-1}, low_t) <= sma50 and close_t > sma50.
items.evidence: Author's examples only.
items.unverified: 'At or below the 50-day' wording via a translated summary.
items.overlap_with_methods_md: Close cousin of the pocket-pivot / MA reclaim ideas in methods/07-08.

items.name: Boomers (and extended-level Boomers)
items.brand_or_source: Jeff Cooper, Hit and Run Trading (ch. 11) and Hit and Run Trading II
items.rules_or_formula: Boomer buy: ADX > 30 with +DI > -DI; the stock makes two consecutive inside days; on the next day buy 10 cents above the high of the second inside day; initial stop 10 cents below the second inside day's low. Extended-level variant: day 1 is a new 60-day high; the next two or more days are inside relative to day 1's range; buy stop 1 tick above the day-1 high; cancel if price trades below the day-1 low. Shorts mirror.
items.entry: Stop above inside-day cluster
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact on daily bars.
items.evidence: None beyond author examples.
items.unverified: Rules come from a search summary of scan-forum and screener pages, not the book.

items.name: Lizards
items.brand_or_source: Jeff Cooper, Hit and Run Trading, ch. 14
items.rules_or_formula: Bullish lizard: today makes a new 10-day low but both the open and the close are in the top 25% of the day's range (long lower tail). Next day: buy stop above the lizard bar's high (aggressive: buy the open). Stop below the lizard low. Bearish mirror: new 10-day high with open and close in the bottom 25% of the range.
items.entry: Stop above lizard high
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact: low_t == min(low_{t-9..t}) and (open-low)/(range) >= 0.75 and (close-low)/(range) >= 0.75.
items.evidence: None beyond author examples.

items.name: Landry Bow Tie, Proper Order and Percent-of-Close trend rules
items.brand_or_source: Dave Landry (Dave Landry on Swing Trading; Trading Simplified plug-in docs)
items.rules_or_formula: Averages: 10 SMA, 20 EMA, 30 EMA. Proper Order up = 10 SMA > 20 EMA > 30 EMA (down = reverse; anything else = choppy, 'yellow'). Bow Tie = the three averages converge/cross and then fan out into proper order, marking a new trend; then wait for the first pullback (Landry pullback: >= 2 bars of lower lows, buy above the prior bar's high). Landry Light: uptrend while each bar's low is above the MA (default 50 SMA; reference 40 bars of trend age). 10% TFM long-term rule: long while price is above the 'Percent of Close' line = 90% of the highest close of the last 50 bars (i.e., within 10% of the 50-day closing high).
items.entry: First pullback after a bow tie
items.exit: Landry 2-for-1: half off at 1R, trail rest
items.daily_bar_implementation: All codeable; needs ema_30 feature.
items.evidence: No independent test; pullback family B- per methods/01.
items.overlap_with_methods_md: Proper Order, Landry Light and pullback >= 2 lower lows already in methods/01; new here: bow-tie sequencing and the 90%-of-50-day-closing-high rule.

items.name: Trend Knockout (TKO)
items.brand_or_source: Dave Landry (StockCharts 'Trading Simplified', 6 Nov 2019)
items.rules_or_formula: In an established strong trend, wait for a wide-range bar AGAINST the trend that shakes out late buyers (often undercutting recent lows). Entry: buy when price trades back above the high of that counter-trend wide-range bar (trend resumption traps the new shorts). Stop below the TKO bar's low. If the trend has truly ended the trigger usually never fires.
items.entry: Stop above the shakeout bar's high
items.daily_bar_implementation: Codeable: trend filter (Proper Order) + bar range > k x ATR with close < open and low < prior low; trigger = high > that bar's high within N days.
items.evidence: None.
items.unverified: Wide-range threshold and trigger window are not defined in what was read.

items.name: Wyckoff accumulation: spring, test, SOS, LPS entries
items.brand_or_source: Richard D. Wyckoff (method as taught by Wyckoff Analytics / StockCharts tutorial)
items.rules_or_formula: Events: PS (preliminary support), SC (selling climax: wide spread, heavy volume, close off the low), AR (automatic rally; its high = top of trading range), ST (secondary test near SC on lower volume and spread), spring/shakeout (price breaks below the TR low then reverses to close back inside), test (retest of spring low on low volume), SOS (advance on widening spread and higher volume), LPS (pullback on lower spread/volume to former resistance), BU (back-up after the SOS). Phases A (stop of decline) -> B (building cause) -> C (spring/test) -> D (SOSs and LPSs) -> E (markup). Entries: buy a successful spring test (Phase C) or the LPS/BU after an SOS (Phase D). Nine buying tests include: downside P&F objective met; PS/SC/ST present; volume rising on rallies and falling on reactions; downtrend line broken; higher lows; higher highs; stock stronger than the market; base forming; upside potential >= 3x the initial risk. Market five-step: trend of market, stocks in harmony and stronger, enough 'cause' (P&F count), readiness (nine tests), time with index turn.
items.entry: Spring test or LPS
items.daily_bar_implementation: Approximation: TR = rolling 40-120 day box; spring = low < TR low and close > TR low; test = later low >= spring low on volume < 20-day average; SOS = close > AR high with volume > 1.5x average; LPS = pullback holding above TR top on falling volume.
items.data_needed: Daily OHLCV (+ index for relative strength)
items.evidence: No independent quantitative test located.
items.overlap_with_methods_md: Kell (methods/12) borrows the cycle vocabulary; no Wyckoff module exists.

items.name: Wyckoff distribution: UT/UTAD, SOW, LPSY (exit/short tool)
items.brand_or_source: Richard D. Wyckoff
items.rules_or_formula: PSY (preliminary supply), BC (buying climax, often on good news), AR (automatic reaction; its low = TR floor), ST (test of BC on lower volume; may be an upthrust UT), SOW (drop to or through TR support on wider spread and volume), LPSY (feeble, narrow-spread rally after a SOW), UTAD (upthrust after distribution: break above TR resistance that fails back into range). Phase D: break of support or fall below TR midpoint after a UT/UTAD. Selling tests include: upside objective met; volume falling on rallies, rising on reactions; PSY/BC present; stock weaker than market; uptrend line broken; lower highs. Use: exit longs on UTAD failure or SOW; never buy breakouts that fail back into a distribution range.
items.evidence: None quantitative.

items.name: Weinstein Stage Analysis: Stage 2 breakout (trader method) and continuation buys
items.brand_or_source: Stan Weinstein, Secrets for Profiting in Bull and Bear Markets (1988)
items.rules_or_formula: Weekly charts, 30-week SMA. Stage 1 base: declines stop, price goes sideways, 30-week MA flattens. Stage 2 advance: price above a rising 30-week MA, higher highs/lows, volume up on rallies. Stage 3 top: MA flattens, price chops around it. Stage 4 decline: below a falling MA. Buy (trader method): weekly close above the Stage 1 resistance/top of base, price above the 30-week MA that has stopped falling (ideally turning up); breakout-week volume at least 2x the average of the prior 4 weeks (stageanalysis.net also accepts 3x average daily volume on the breakout day); Mansfield RS above or crossing above its zero line; little overhead resistance nearby. Investor method: buy the first pullback toward the breakout level/30-week MA. Continuation buys: later Stage 2 bases breaking out with the same checks. Stops: below the base/last correction low under the breakout, then raise below each new correction low; investors trail under the rising 30-week MA. Sell/short: Stage 4 breakdowns below support and a declining MA.
items.entry: Weekly close above base with volume and RS
items.daily_bar_implementation: Use weekly bars (resample) or daily 150-day SMA equivalent; volume test on weekly sums.
items.evidence: No independent test of the full method found (methods.md rates D). The 30-week/10-month trend filter has B evidence for drawdown control (methods.md row 1).
items.unverified: Stop-placement details from the book were not re-read this run.
items.overlap_with_methods_md: methods.md 1b lists Weinstein as a candidate weekly strategy; this adds the explicit buy checklist.

items.name: Mansfield Relative Strength
items.brand_or_source: Mansfield Charts / Stan Weinstein
items.rules_or_formula: RP = stock close / index close (weekly). Mansfield RS = (RP / SMA_52(RP) - 1) x 100. Zero line = RP equal to its 52-week average. Above zero and rising = outperforming; Weinstein wants it positive or crossing up at a Stage 2 breakout and avoids buys with negative RS.
items.data_needed: Weekly closes of stock and benchmark
items.evidence: RS/momentum ranking itself is A-grade (methods.md row 2); this normalisation is untested on its own.

items.name: Darvas Box
items.brand_or_source: Nicolas Darvas, How I Made $2,000,000 in the Stock Market (1960)
items.rules_or_formula: Universe: stocks at new highs (52-week), on rising volume, preferably with improving earnings ('techno-fundamentalist'). Box top: a new high that is not exceeded on the next 3 consecutive days. Box bottom: after the top is set, the lowest low that holds for 3 consecutive days. Buy: price breaks above the box top (buy stop just above it; many codings require a close above and buy next open) with volume expansion (one coding: breakout volume >= 1.3x the box-period average). Stop: just below the box bottom. Pyramid: buy more when a new, higher box forms and breaks; move the shared stop to the bottom of the latest box. Exit all on a break below the current box bottom.
items.entry: Break above box top on volume
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact state machine on daily bars (top confirm 3 days, bottom confirm 3 days).
items.data_needed: Daily OHLCV (+ EPS for the fundamental leg)
items.evidence: Book anecdote; no independent test located. Related evidence: Wilcox & Crittenden (2005) all-time-high breakouts with ATR trailing stops on 24,000+ US stocks had positive expectancy; Zarattini, Pagani & Wilcox (2025) extended it to 1950-2024, 66,000+ trades, <7% of trades produce the profit.

items.name: Turtle breakout systems (System 1: 20/10, System 2: 55/20)
items.brand_or_source: Richard Dennis & William Eckhardt; rules published by Curtis Faith ('The Original Turtle Trading Rules', Way of the Turtle 2007)
items.rules_or_formula: System 1: enter when price exceeds the 20-day high (long) / 20-day low (short) by a tick, intraday stop. Skip the signal if the LAST System-1 breakout (taken or not) would have been a winner; if skipped, still take a 55-day breakout as failsafe. Exit longs on a 10-day low (shorts on a 10-day high). System 2: 55-day breakout, always taken; exit on a 20-day opposite extreme. Initial stop 2N from entry; pyramid one unit every 1/2 N in favour up to 4 units; when a unit is added, all stops move to 2N from the newest entry. Whipsaw variant: 1/2 N stop with re-entry.
items.entry: Stop at 20/55-day extreme
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact on daily bars; the skip filter needs a shadow-trade ledger.
items.evidence: Futures trend-following evidence is strong; for stocks the closest test is Wilcox & Crittenden (2005, long-only ATH breakout + ATR trail: $1,000 grew to ~$30,000 over 22 years on 24,000+ stocks) and Zarattini, Pagani & Wilcox (2025, 1950-2024). Expect <50% winners, edge from a few large winners.

items.name: Turtle N-based sizing, stops and unit limits
items.brand_or_source: Curtis Faith, The Original Turtle Trading Rules
items.rules_or_formula: True range TR = max(H - L, H - prior close, prior close - L). N = (19 x prior N + TR) / 20 (a 20-day Wilder-smoothed ATR). Dollar volatility = N x dollars per point (for stocks, N per share). Unit = 1% of account equity / dollar volatility (so a 1N move = 1% of equity). Limits: 4 units per market, 6 in closely correlated markets, 10 in loosely correlated, 12 per direction (long or short). Stops 2N (= 2% equity per unit). Drawdown rule: for every 10% drawdown, trade as if the account were 20% smaller (until recovered).
items.evidence: Volatility-normalised sizing is standard; vol-scaling evidence is B in methods.md (Barroso & Santa-Clara).
items.unverified: Drawdown rule recalled from the Faith PDF; not re-fetched this run.

items.name: Elder Triple Screen
items.brand_or_source: Alexander Elder (Futures, 1986; Trading for a Living, 1993; Come into My Trading Room, 2002)
items.rules_or_formula: Screen 1 (tide): weekly trend from the slope of the weekly MACD-Histogram (12,26,9) (early versions: slope of a weekly EMA); trade only in that direction. Screen 2 (wave): daily oscillator against the tide - in a weekly uptrend look for 2-day EMA of Force Index below zero (or Stochastic oversold, Williams %R below -80, Elder-ray Bear Power negative but rising). Screen 3 (ripple/entry): trailing buy-stop 1 tick above the previous day's high; if not hit, lower it to above the latest day's high each day until filled or the setup is void. Stop: below the low of the entry day or the prior day, whichever is lower (later: SafeZone stops). Money management: risk at most 2% of equity per trade; stop trading for the month once losses reach 6% of equity.
items.entry: Trailing buy stop above prior high
items.daily_bar_implementation: Codeable on daily bars with weekly resampling.
items.evidence: No independent test located.
items.unverified: 2%/6% rules from Elder's 2002 book, not fetched this run.

items.name: Elder Impulse System
items.brand_or_source: Alexander Elder
items.rules_or_formula: Green bar: 13-period EMA rising AND MACD-Histogram (12,26,9) rising. Red bar: both falling. Blue: mixed. Use two timeframes (long = intermediate x 5, e.g., weekly for daily trading): buy only when the long-term trend is bullish and the daily impulse turns green (no buying on red bars); shorts mirror. 'Enter cautiously, exit fast': exit when the bar colour turns against the position.
items.evidence: None independent.

items.name: Elder Force Index
items.brand_or_source: Alexander Elder
items.rules_or_formula: FI(1) = (close - prior close) x volume. FI(2) = 2-day EMA of FI(1) (short-term pullback timing: buy when it turns negative in an uptrend defined by a rising 22-day EMA; exit when it turns back positive). FI(13) = 13-day EMA (intermediate trend, divergences). FI(100) for long trends.
items.evidence: None independent.

items.name: Bollinger Method I (Squeeze breakout) and Method IV (confirmed breakout)
items.brand_or_source: John Bollinger, Bollinger on Bollinger Bands (2001); Method IV added later (TradeStation manuals, 2021)
items.rules_or_formula: Bands: middle = SMA(close, 20); upper/lower = middle +/- 2 x stdev(close, 20). BandWidth = (upper - lower) / middle (x100 on StockCharts). Squeeze: BandWidth near the low end of its ~6-month range (a scan proxy: (upper - lower)/close < 0.04). Method I: after a squeeze, go with the band break (close above upper = long; below lower = short); best when the squeeze is brief and the break quick; beware the 'head fake' (first break reverses) - use volume indicators (Intraday Intensity, A/D, MFI, OBV, CMF) inside the squeeze to anticipate direction. Method IV: requires CONSECUTIVE closes outside the band after a squeeze and uses ADX to judge whether the market is trending. Stops: Parabolic SAR or failure back inside the bands (practitioner).
items.entry: Close outside band after squeeze (IV: 2 closes)
items.daily_bar_implementation: Codeable; BandWidth percentile over 126 bars <= 5-10% as the squeeze flag.
items.evidence: Lento, Gradojevic & Wright (2007): Bollinger Band rules did not beat buy-and-hold after costs (contrarian versions did better) - tested band-touch rules, not the squeeze. No independent squeeze test verified.
items.unverified: Exact Method IV ADX threshold not stated in the manual excerpt.

items.name: Bollinger Method II (%b + MFI trend following)
items.brand_or_source: John Bollinger, Bollinger on Bollinger Bands (2001)
items.rules_or_formula: Buy when %b > 0.8 AND MFI(10) > 80 (strong price confirmed by strong money flow); sell/short when %b < 0.2 AND MFI(10) < 20. Bollinger suggests Parabolic SAR for stops. ChartSchool tweaks: require a low ADX (< 15) before the signal (new trend emerging) and enter on the first pullback when MACD crosses its signal line.
items.entry: %b>0.8 and MFI>80
items.daily_bar_implementation: Codeable.
items.evidence: See Lento et al. (2007); method-specific test not found.

items.name: Bollinger Method III (reversals with Intraday Intensity) and W-bottoms
items.brand_or_source: John Bollinger
items.rules_or_formula: Buy alert: price tags the lower band while Intraday Intensity is positive (volume-weighted close location; II = (2C - H - L)/(H - L) x V, used as a 21-day normalised II%). Sell alert: upper-band tag while II is negative. These are alerts, not signals: wait for confirmation (a strong up bar after a buy alert). W-bottom: first low closes outside/at the lower band; the retest low holds inside the band (higher %b) - buy the break above the intervening peak. Rules: tags are not signals; closes outside the bands are initially continuation signals.
items.entry: Confirmation bar after alert
items.daily_bar_implementation: Codeable.
items.evidence: None independent.
items.unverified: Exact II% normalisation formula not in the manual excerpt.

items.name: %b and BandWidth (Bollinger indicators and 22 rules)
items.brand_or_source: John Bollinger
items.rules_or_formula: %b = (price - lower band)/(upper band - lower band): 1 at upper band, 0 at lower, 0.5 at middle. BandWidth = (upper - lower)/middle (equals 4x the coefficient of variation at default settings). Defaults 20 periods / 2 stdev; for similar containment use 2.1 stdev at 50 periods and 1.9 at 10. Simple MA bands are standard; exponential bands need EMA for both mean and stdev. Rules: tags are not signals; prices can walk the bands; closes outside are initially continuation signals; normalise other indicators with 50+ period bands and their %b.
items.evidence: Indicator definitions.

items.name: TTM Squeeze
items.brand_or_source: John Carter, Mastering the Trade (Trade the Markets / Simpler Trading)
items.rules_or_formula: Squeeze ON when the Bollinger Bands (20, 2 stdev) are inside the Keltner Channel (20-period average +/- 1.5 x ATR(20); StockCharts uses Keltner's original formula for this): upper BB < upper KC and lower BB > lower KC. Squeeze FIRES when the bands move back outside the channel. Momentum histogram = linear regression (20) of [close - ((highest high_20 + lowest low_20)/2 + SMA_20(close))/2]. Trade: on the first 'fired' bar after one or more squeeze bars, buy if momentum is above zero and rising (short if below zero and falling). Exit after two consecutive bars of fading momentum (two darker bars); moves typically last 8-10 bars.
items.entry: First fired bar in momentum direction
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact on daily bars.
items.evidence: No independent test located.

items.name: Keltner Channels (original 1960 and Raschke version)
items.brand_or_source: Chester Keltner, How to Make Money in Commodities (1960); modern version by Linda Raschke (1980s)
items.rules_or_formula: Original: centre = 10-day SMA of typical price (H+L+C)/3; bands = centre +/- 10-day SMA of (high - low); Keltner's rule: buy a close above the upper line, sell below the lower ('ten-day moving average rule'). Modern: 20-day EMA +/- 2 x ATR(10). Signals: channel turning up plus a break above the upper line = new uptrend; in flat channels the lines act as overbought/oversold. Multiplier 1 halves width, 3 widens by 50%.
items.evidence: None independent verified.

items.name: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo (cloud) trend and pullback rules
items.brand_or_source: Goichi Hosoda (published 1969)
items.rules_or_formula: Tenkan = (9-period high + 9-period low)/2; Kijun = (26H + 26L)/2; Senkou A = (Tenkan + Kijun)/2 plotted 26 periods ahead; Senkou B = (52H + 52L)/2 plotted 26 ahead; Chikou = close plotted 26 back. Trend up above the cloud, down below, flat inside; green cloud when Span A > Span B. Signals: Tenkan crosses above Kijun in an uptrend (stronger above a green cloud); price-Kijun crosses; chikou above price of 26 bars ago confirms. ChartSchool pullback system: bullish bias while price is above the lower cloud line; pullback = price drops below Kijun; entry = price crosses back above Tenkan; stop at the low before the signal; trail with Parabolic SAR or 2 ATR.
items.entry: Tenkan reclaim after Kijun dip in bullish bias
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact; beware look-ahead with the 26-bar forward plot (use spans computed 26 bars ago).
items.evidence: No peer-reviewed test verified this run.
items.unverified: Hosoda's own time-cycle rules (9/17/26 counts, wave and price targets) not covered.

items.name: Supertrend
items.brand_or_source: Attributed to Olivier Seban
items.rules_or_formula: median = (H + L)/2; basic upper = median + m x ATR(n); basic lower = median - m x ATR(n); defaults m = 3, n = 10 (TradingView) or 7. Final upper = basic upper if basic upper < prior final upper or prior close > prior final upper, else prior final upper. Final lower = basic lower if basic lower > prior final lower or prior close < prior final lower, else prior final lower. Trend flips up when close > final upper, down when close < final lower; the line is the final lower band in uptrends and final upper in downtrends. Use as trailing stop / trend filter.
items.evidence: None independent.

items.name: Parabolic SAR
items.brand_or_source: J. Welles Wilder, New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems (1978)
items.rules_or_formula: Rising SAR_t = SAR_{t-1} + AF x (EP - SAR_{t-1}), EP = highest high of the current up-move; AF starts 0.02, +0.02 at each new EP, max 0.20. Rising SAR may not exceed the lows of the prior two bars (use the lower). Falling SAR mirrors (EP = lowest low; may not be below the prior two highs). Stop-and-reverse when price penetrates SAR; new SAR starts at the prior EP. Bollinger pairs it with Method II as the stop.
items.evidence: None independent verified.

items.name: Chandelier Exit
items.brand_or_source: Chuck (Charles) LeBeau; popularised in Elder's books
items.rules_or_formula: Long stop = highest high of the last 22 bars - 3 x ATR(22). Short stop = lowest low of 22 bars + 3 x ATR(22). Raise the multiplier for volatile names, lower it for quiet ones. Exit-only tool; pair with a separate entry.
items.evidence: ATR trailing stops are the exit in the Wilcox-Crittenden stock trend tests (positive expectancy); the chandelier itself is untested.

items.name: Heikin-Ashi trend riding
items.brand_or_source: Japanese technique; Dan Valcu, 'Using the Heikin-Ashi Technique', S&C Feb 2004
items.rules_or_formula: HA close = (O + H + L + C)/4; HA open = (prior HA open + prior HA close)/2; HA high = max(H, HA open, HA close); HA low = min(L, HA open, HA close). Riding: stay long while HA candles are up (HA close > HA open), especially with no lower shadows (strong trend); small bodies or long two-sided shadows (HA doji/spinning tops) flag indecision; exit or tighten on the first down HA candle or a confirmed break of the indecision bar. Valcu adds haDiff = HA close - HA open (and its average) as a trend-strength line.
items.entry: First up HA candle with no lower shadow after a down sequence (practitioner)
items.exit: First down HA candle / confirmed reversal
items.daily_bar_implementation: Exact; HA values are synthetic - fill at real prices.
items.evidence: None independent.

items.name: Guppy Multiple Moving Average (GMMA)
items.brand_or_source: Daryl Guppy
items.rules_or_formula: Short group EMAs 3, 5, 8, 10, 12, 15 (traders); long group EMAs 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 60 (investors). Bullish when the short group crosses above the long group; the wider and more parallel the separation, the stronger the trend. Compression of both groups = agreement / no trend (pre-breakout). Pullback entry: in an uptrend the short group dips toward the long group without crossing it, then re-expands; enter on the break above the candle that tested the long ribbon.
items.evidence: None independent.

items.name: Fibonacci retracement pullbacks
items.brand_or_source: Practitioner standard (ChartSchool); Dow/Hamilton 1/3-2/3 rule
items.rules_or_formula: Levels = swing high - r x (swing high - swing low) for r = 0.236, 0.382, 0.5, 0.618 (0.786 popular). They are alert zones, not signals: buy only on confirmation (reversal candle, oscillator turn, MA reclaim) inside the 38.2-61.8% zone of a prior impulse in an uptrend; stop beyond the 61.8-78.6% level or the swing low. Hamilton (Dow theory) observed secondary moves retrace 1/3-2/3 of the primary move, typically about 50%.
items.evidence: No peer-reviewed evidence that Fibonacci ratios beat arbitrary levels was verified this run.

items.name: Floor pivot points (standard, Fibonacci, DeMark)
items.brand_or_source: Floor-trader tradition (ChartSchool)
items.rules_or_formula: Standard: P = (H + L + C)/3; S1 = 2P - H; R1 = 2P - L; S2 = P - (H - L); R2 = P + (H - L); common R3 = H + 2(P - L), S3 = L - 2(H - P). Fibonacci: S/R1 = P -/+ 0.382 x (H - L); S/R2 = P -/+ 0.618 x (H - L); S/R3 = P -/+ 1.0 x (H - L). DeMark pivots depend on close vs open and give one R1/S1. Timeframes: intraday charts use the prior day's HLC; StockCharts daily charts use the prior month's HLC; weekly/monthly charts use the prior year's. Swing use: monthly (or weekly) pivots as targets/stop references, P as bias line.
items.evidence: No equity swing test verified.
items.unverified: Standard R3/S3 formula is the common convention, not shown on the ChartSchool page.

items.name: Gap trading and gap-fill fades
items.brand_or_source: ChartSchool gap trading strategies; gap-fill statistics (TradeThatSwing, thetrading.tools)
items.rules_or_formula: Types: full gap up = open > prior high; partial gap up = open > prior close but <= prior high (mirror for downs). ChartSchool eight rules: let the first hour set a range, then go long on a buy stop 2 ticks above the first-hour high or short on a sell stop 2 ticks below the first-hour low; for a full gap down a long stop 2 ticks above the prior day's low (an Oops-type rule); trailing stops of 8% (long) / 4% (short), tighter 5-6% for partial gaps. Fade logic: small opening gaps in index ETFs usually fill (prior close) the same day; large gaps usually do not and are better treated as continuation (see methods/13 PEG).
items.data_needed: Daily OHLC (first-hour bars for ChartSchool rules)
items.evidence: Descriptive stats: SPY up-gaps of 0.1-0.25% filled same day about 78% of the time; 0.25-0.5% gaps about 60% same day and 82% within 5 sessions; ES gaps > 1.2x ATR(14) filled same day only about 8% (2014-2024). No cost-inclusive swing test.
items.unverified: Fill percentages are from search summaries of those pages.

items.name: Inside-bar and outside-bar breakouts
items.brand_or_source: Classic bar patterns (Williams; Crabel)
items.rules_or_formula: Inside bar: high < prior high and low > prior low. Outside bar: high > prior high and low < prior low. Inside-bar breakout: buy stop above the inside bar (or the 'mother' bar) high, stop below the low; best in the trend direction or combined with NR4/NR7 (see ID/NR4). Outside bar: direction set by the close (bullish outside bar closing near its high = continuation/reversal up; enter above its high). Williams ignores inside days when marking swing points. Frequencies (Williams, 9 commodities, 50,692 sessions): inside days 7.6%, outside days 3,487 sessions.
items.evidence: No robust stand-alone test verified; NR7/ID-NR4 tests are the closest (C).

items.name: Key reversal day
items.brand_or_source: Classic futures-pit pattern
items.rules_or_formula: Bearish: in an uptrend, price makes a new high above the prior bar's high, then closes below the prior close (strict: below the prior low). Bullish: new low below the prior low, then close above the prior close (strict: above the prior high). Wider range and heavier volume are said to strengthen it. Entry: next-day break of the reversal bar's extreme; stop beyond the reversal bar.
items.evidence: Weak: SentimenTrader found the Nasdaq positive only 41% of the time a month after a key reversal; a study of ~600 downward key reversals across ~1,470 stocks found no lasting trend prediction; StoneX (18 Aug 2026) found bullish key reversals in ASX 200 futures anticipated the move 2-4 sessions out.

items.name: Dow Theory confirmation (regime)
items.brand_or_source: Charles Dow, William P. Hamilton, Robert Rhea
items.rules_or_formula: Identify each average's trend by peaks and troughs: an uptrend stays valid until a lower low forms and the following decline breaks the prior reaction low (downtrend mirrors: higher low then a rally above the prior reaction high). Hamilton ignored moves under ~3%. Both averages must confirm: a bull signal needs new reaction highs in BOTH the Dow Industrials and the Dow Transports; divergence = warning, not reversal. Secondary moves retrace 1/3-2/3 (typically ~50%), are sharper than primaries, end with a dull low-volume period; volume should expand with the primary trend. 'Lines' = sideways ranges whose breakout sets direction. Swing use: market gate (long only while DJIA and DJTA are in confirmed primary uptrend).
items.data_needed: Daily closes of DJIA and DJTA (or proxies DIA/IYT)
items.evidence: Brown, Goetzmann & Kumar (Journal of Finance, Aug 1998): Hamilton's 1902-1929 calls earned positive risk-adjusted returns; a neural-net model of his calls beat buy-and-hold by about 4.4 pp a year over 1930-1997.

items.name: Pring KST (Know Sure Thing)
items.brand_or_source: Martin Pring (S&C 1992)
items.rules_or_formula: RCMA1 = SMA10(ROC10); RCMA2 = SMA10(ROC15); RCMA3 = SMA10(ROC20); RCMA4 = SMA15(ROC30); KST = 1xRCMA1 + 2xRCMA2 + 3xRCMA3 + 4xRCMA4; signal = SMA9(KST). Daily KST(10,15,20,30,10,10,10,15,9); weekly KST(10,13,15,20,10,13,15,20,9); monthly KST(9,12,18,24,6,6,6,9,9). Signals: zero-line and signal-line crossovers (most robust); be careful with bearish signal crossovers in strong uptrends; divergences selectively.
items.evidence: None independent.

items.name: Coppock Curve
items.brand_or_source: Edwin 'Sedge' Coppock, Barron's (Oct 1965)
items.rules_or_formula: Monthly data: Coppock = 10-period weighted MA of (14-month ROC + 11-month ROC). Buy when it crosses from below zero to above zero (Coppock used buys only; sells on a cross below zero are a later addition). Very few signals (about five on monthly data since the late 1980s per ChartSchool). Can be re-scaled to weekly/daily for more signals.
items.evidence: None independent verified.

items.name: Dorsey Wright point-and-figure relative strength and Technical Attribute
items.brand_or_source: Dorsey Wright & Associates (Nasdaq Dorsey Wright); Tom Dorsey, Point & Figure Charting
items.rules_or_formula: RS line = (stock close / benchmark close) x 100 (benchmark often the S&P 500 Equal Weight), plotted as a 3-box-reversal P&F chart. RS buy signal: an X column exceeds the prior X column (double top); RS sell: an O column breaks the prior O column; RS signals reportedly last about 18-24 months on average. RS Matrix: chart every pair in a universe and rank each security by how many of its pairwise RS charts are on buy signals. Technical Attribute score 0-5: two attributes versus the market, two versus sector peers, one absolute trend attribute (exact composition and RS box size not confirmed this run).
items.data_needed: Daily closes of stocks, sector and benchmark
items.evidence: Real-money proxy: Invesco DWA Momentum ETF (PDP) about 11-12%/yr over 10 years, behind the S&P 500 (aggregator figures). Cross-sectional momentum itself is A-grade (methods.md).
items.unverified: Box size (commonly quoted 6.5% or 3.25%) and the five-attribute definitions; PDP numbers.

items.name: Sector rotation by relative strength (Faber)
items.brand_or_source: Mebane Faber, 'Relative Strength Strategies for Investing' (white paper); ChartSchool implementation
items.rules_or_formula: Monthly. Market filter: be invested only while the S&P 500 is above its 10-month SMA (exit everything on a monthly close below; a 12-month SMA tweak held trends better). Rank sectors by 3-month ROC (window can be 1-12 months); hold the top 3 equal-weighted (33% each); rebalance monthly, replacing sectors that drop out of the top 3. Faber used 10 Fama-French/CRSP industry groups from the 1920s; a simple momentum rule beat buy-and-hold about 70% of the time over 80+ years.
items.data_needed: Monthly closes of 11 sector ETFs + SPY
items.evidence: Faber's 80-year backtest (in-sample, no costs); industry momentum is a documented anomaly. methods.md rates sector/theme rotation C as a stand-alone system.
items.overlap_with_methods_md: methods.md 1b: use group RS as a ranking input; this adds the exact Faber rules.

items.name: Pre-holiday effect
items.brand_or_source: Stock Trader's Almanac tradition; Ariel (JF 1990)
items.rules_or_formula: Buy one or two trading days before each of the US exchange holidays and sell just after the holiday (short-term version); half-days (day before July 4, day after Thanksgiving) are thin and volatile. Original research: 419 holiday closings, 1928-1975 (S&P 500).
items.evidence: Ariel (1990): the pre-holiday day averaged 9-14x the mean return of other days. Extension to 1983-2019 (Critical Finance Review): the effect now survives only in small firms; large firms show no significant pre-holiday premium, especially after 1990.

items.name: Halloween / Sell in May seasonal
items.brand_or_source: Bouman & Jacobsen (American Economic Review, 2002)
items.rules_or_formula: Hold equities from the end of October to the end of April; reduce or exit (T-bills) from May to October. Use as an exposure overlay (e.g., smaller position sizes or stricter gates in May-October), not as a stand-alone swing entry.
items.evidence: Effect present in 36 of 37 markets, 1970-1998 (Bouman & Jacobsen); UK evidence back to 1694 (Jacobsen & Zhang). Peer-reviewed and replicated, though returns in the 'weak' half are usually still positive.

items.name: Santa Claus rally window
items.brand_or_source: Yale & Jeffrey Hirsch, Stock Trader's Almanac (first published 1972)
items.rules_or_formula: Window = the last 5 trading days of December plus the first 2 trading days of January (7 sessions). Long the index for the window; Almanac lore treats a failed Santa rally as a bearish omen for the new year.
items.evidence: S&P 500 averaged about +1.3% over the window since 1950 (Almanac figures via Bankrate/TradingView); not cost-tested here.
items.overlap_with_methods_md: Turn-of-month seasonality is already in methods.md 1b; not repeated here.
